questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of epithelial tissue?

options.explanation: Epithelial tissue has very little extracellular matrix; that's a feature of connective tissue.
Epithelia are avascular; they receive nutrients via diffusion from underlying connective tissue.

options.text: Polarity with apical and basal surfaces
options.explanation: Epithelial cells exhibit polarity: an apical surface facing the lumen or external environment, and a basal surface attached to the basement membrane.
Epithelia contain multiple junction types, not only gap junctions.
Epithelia originate from all three germ layers.

explanation.overview: Epithelial tissue covers body surfaces, lines cavities, and forms glands. Its cells are tightly packed with little extracellular matrix, exhibit polarity, and rest on a basement membrane.
explanation.highYield: Epithelium = cellular, avascular, polarized, basement membrane, cohesive.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Loss of epithelial polarity is a hallmark of carcinoma progression.

questions.question: The basement membrane is composed of which two layers?

options.explanation: Collagen fibers are in the reticular lamina, but the two layers are basal lamina and reticular lamina.
The basement membrane consists of the basal lamina (produced by epithelium) and the reticular lamina (produced by connective tissue).
Elastic fibers are not the main second layer.
These are ECM components, not the two layers.

explanation.overview: The basement membrane is a specialized extracellular matrix, composed of a basal lamina (laminin, type IV collagen, proteoglycans) from epithelial cells and a reticular lamina (type III collagen) from connective tissue.
explanation.highYield: Basement membrane: basal lamina (epithelium) + reticular lamina (connective tissue).
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Invasive carcinoma breaches the basement membrane.

questions.question: Which type of epithelium is best suited for diffusion and filtration?

options.explanation: Stratified epithelia are thick and protective, not for diffusion.
Simple squamous epithelium consists of a single layer of flat cells, allowing rapid diffusion of gases and fluids, as seen in lung alveoli and capillary endothelium.
Cuboidal cells are thicker, less suited for diffusion.
Taller cells, not for rapid diffusion.

explanation.overview: Simple squamous epithelium forms a thin, flat sheet that facilitates passive diffusion and filtration. It lines blood vessels (endothelium), alveoli, and Bowman's capsule.
explanation.highYield: Simple squamous = thin, flat, diffusion; alveoli, endothelium.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Thickening of alveolar epithelium impairs gas exchange in pulmonary fibrosis.

questions.question: The epithelium lining the urinary bladder is:

options.explanation: Esophagus is stratified squamous, not bladder.
Transitional epithelium (urothelium) lines the urinary tract and stretches to accommodate urine volume changes.

explanation.overview: Transitional epithelium (urothelium) is a stratified epithelium with dome-shaped surface umbrella cells. It transitions from 5-6 layers when relaxed to 2-3 layers when stretched.
explanation.highYield: Bladder = transitional (urothelium); umbrella cells; stretches.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Urothelial carcinoma is the most common bladder cancer.

questions.question: Goblet cells are found in which type of epithelium?

options.explanation: Goblet cells are unicellular mucous glands typically found in simple columnar epithelium of the respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts.
Keratinized epithelium is for protection, not secretion.

explanation.overview: Goblet cells are modified columnar epithelial cells that secrete mucin. They are scattered among other columnar cells in the intestines and respiratory tract.
explanation.highYield: Goblet cells = simple/pseudostratified columnar; mucus secretion.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Goblet cell metaplasia in airways occurs in chronic bronchitis and asthma.

questions.question: Keratinized stratified squamous epithelium is found in:

options.explanation: Oral mucosa is non-keratinized (except hard palate and gingiva).
The epidermis of the skin is keratinized to provide a waterproof barrier against the environment.

explanation.overview: Keratinized stratified squamous epithelium has dead surface cells filled with keratin, providing a tough, dry protective layer. It is unique to the skin (epidermis).
explanation.highYield: Keratinized stratified squamous = epidermis; waterproof, protective.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Psoriasis involves abnormal keratinization with parakeratosis (nuclei in stratum corneum).

questions.question: Microvilli are specialized structures that increase surface area for absorption and are found on:

options.explanation: Ciliated cells have cilia, not microvilli.

options.text: Brush border of intestinal epithelial cells
options.explanation: Intestinal epithelial cells have a brush border of microvilli to maximize nutrient absorption.

options.text: Basal surface of all epithelial cells

explanation.overview: Microvilli are cytoplasmic projections containing actin filaments that increase apical surface area. They are prominent in the small intestine (striated/brush border) and proximal kidney tubule.
explanation.highYield: Microvilli = brush border (intestine), striated border (kidney); actin core.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Celiac disease leads to loss of microvilli (villous atrophy) and malabsorption.

questions.question: Cilia are motile structures found on epithelial cells of the:

options.explanation: Proximal tubule has microvilli, not cilia.
Ciliated epithelium lines the respiratory tract, where cilia move mucus and trapped particles toward the pharynx.
Stomach has simple columnar with mucus, not cilia.

explanation.overview: Motile cilia contain a 9+2 microtubule axoneme and dynein arms, generating rhythmic beating. They line the respiratory tract (mucociliary clearance), fallopian tubes, and central nervous system ventricles.
explanation.highYield: Cilia = respiratory tract, fallopian tubes; 9+2 structure; mucociliary escalator.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (Kartagener's syndrome) causes chronic respiratory infections and infertility.

questions.question: The type of cell junction that prevents paracellular leakage is the:

options.explanation: Gap junctions allow communication, not sealing.
Tight junctions seal adjacent epithelial cells, preventing diffusion of molecules between cells.
Adherens junctions link actin, not seal.

explanation.overview: Tight junctions (zonula occludens) form a continuous belt around the apical pole of epithelial cells, fusing the plasma membranes of adjacent cells. They create a semipermeable barrier controlling paracellular transport.
explanation.highYield: Tight junction = seal; claudins and occludins; prevents leakage.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Clostridium perfringens enterotoxin disrupts tight junctions, causing diarrhea.

questions.question: Which junction provides mechanical strength by anchoring intermediate filaments?

options.explanation: Tight junctions seal, not anchor intermediate filaments.
Desmosomes attach to keratin intermediate filaments and provide strong adhesion between cells, especially in tissues under mechanical stress.
Adherens junctions link actin, not intermediate filaments.

explanation.overview: Desmosomes are plaque-like junctions where cadherins (desmogleins, desmocollins) link to keratin intermediate filaments, distributing mechanical stress across the epithelium. They are abundant in epidermis and cardiac muscle.
explanation.highYield: Desmosome = intermediate filament anchor; desmogleins; strong adhesion.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Pemphigus vulgaris involves autoantibodies against desmoglein 3, causing blistering.

questions.question: Hemidesmosomes attach epithelial cells to the:

options.explanation: Hemidesmosomes anchor the basal surface of epithelial cells to the underlying basement membrane.
They attach to the basement membrane, not directly to cells.

explanation.overview: Hemidesmosomes are half-desmosomes on the basal surface of epithelial cells. Integrin α6β4 and plectin link keratin intermediate filaments to laminin in the basement membrane.
explanation.highYield: Hemidesmosome = anchor to basal lamina; integrins + laminin.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Bullous pemphigoid is caused by autoantibodies against BP180/BP230 in hemidesmosomes.

questions.question: Gap junctions allow for:

options.text: Ionic and small molecule passage between cells
options.explanation: Gap junctions form channels that permit direct diffusion of ions and small molecules, enabling electrical and metabolic coupling.

explanation.overview: Gap junctions are clusters of channels (connexons) made of connexin proteins. They allow direct electrical and metabolic coupling between cells by passing ions, cAMP, and small molecules (<1 kDa).
explanation.highYield: Gap junction = connexin/connexon; direct cell-cell communication.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Connexin mutations cause Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (Cx32) and congenital deafness (Cx26).

questions.question: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium appears stratified because:

options.text: Cells are arranged in multiple layers
Nuclei are at different heights, but all cells contact the basement membrane
options.explanation: In pseudostratified epithelium, all cells rest on the basement membrane, but their nuclei are located at varying levels, giving a false stratified appearance.

options.text: There are multiple cell types stacked

options.explanation: Goblet cells are present but not the cause of pseudostratification.
Not all pseudostratified epithelia are ciliated.

explanation.overview: Pseudostratified columnar epithelium is a simple epithelium where all cells touch the basement membrane, but nuclei are at varying heights, creating a false impression of stratification. It lines much of the respiratory tract.
explanation.highYield: Pseudostratified = all cells on basement membrane, nuclei at different levels.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Smoking causes metaplasia of respiratory pseudostratified epithelium to stratified squamous.

questions.question: Which epithelium lines the stomach and intestines?

options.explanation: Simple columnar epithelium lines the stomach and intestines, where it functions in secretion and absorption.

explanation.overview: The mucosa of the stomach and intestines is lined by simple columnar epithelium, specialized for absorption (enterocytes with microvilli) and secretion (goblet cells, gastric glands).
explanation.highYield: GI tract lining = simple columnar; absorption and secretion.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Intestinal metaplasia of the stomach (e.g., in chronic gastritis) is a risk factor for adenocarcinoma.

questions.question: The epithelium of the esophagus is:

options.explanation: The esophagus is lined by non‑keratinized stratified squamous epithelium to protect against abrasion.

explanation.overview: The esophagus is subjected to friction from swallowed food and is lined by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which protects while remaining moist.
explanation.highYield: Esophagus = non-keratinized stratified squamous.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Barrett's esophagus is a metaplastic change to columnar epithelium due to chronic reflux.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of epithelial tissue?

options.explanation: Support is primarily a function of connective tissue. Epithelium covers surfaces, lines cavities, and forms glands.

explanation.overview: Epithelial functions include protection (skin), absorption (intestine), secretion (glands), filtration (kidney), and sensation (neuroepithelium). Structural support is the role of connective tissue.
explanation.highYield: Epithelium: cover, line, absorb, secrete, sense; NOT structural support.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Loss of epithelial barrier function leads to dehydration and infection.

questions.question: The term 'endothelium' refers to epithelium lining:

options.explanation: Alveoli have simple squamous, but 'endothelium' specifically means blood/lymphatic vessel lining.
Endothelium is the simple squamous epithelium that lines the interior of blood vessels, lymphatics, and the heart.
GI has simple columnar, not endothelium.

explanation.overview: Endothelium is a specialized simple squamous epithelium that forms the inner lining of the entire cardiovascular system (including capillaries) and lymphatic vessels.
explanation.highYield: Endothelium = blood vessels, lymphatics; simple squamous.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Endothelial dysfunction is a key step in atherosclerosis.

questions.question: Mesothelium lines:

options.explanation: Mesothelium is the simple squamous epithelium lining serous cavities (pleura, pericardium, peritoneum).

explanation.overview: Mesothelium is a simple squamous epithelium that lines the pericardial, pleural, and peritoneal cavities, reducing friction by secreting serous fluid.
explanation.highYield: Mesothelium = serous cavities; simple squamous; secretes lubricating fluid.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Mesothelioma is a rare malignancy of mesothelial cells, often linked to asbestos exposure.

questions.question: Which of the following glands secretes its product by exocytosis without loss of cellular material?

options.explanation: Apocrine involves pinching off apical cytoplasm.
Merocrine (eccrine) glands release secretions via exocytosis, leaving the cell intact. Examples: salivary glands, pancreatic acini.
Mammary gland protein secretion is merocrine, but lipid secretion is apocrine.

explanation.overview: Merocrine secretion is the most common type, where secretory vesicles fuse with the plasma membrane and release their contents by exocytosis, without cell damage. Pancreatic acinar cells, salivary glands, and most sweat glands use this mode.
explanation.highYield: Merocrine = exocytosis, no cell loss; pancreas, salivary glands.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Cystic fibrosis affects merocrine secretion in sweat glands (elevated Cl⁻ in sweat test).

questions.question: In holocrine secretion, the entire cell disintegrates to release its product. An example is:

options.explanation: Sebaceous glands are holocrine: cells accumulate lipid and rupture, releasing sebum.

explanation.overview: Holocrine secretion involves the programmed death of the secretory cell, which fills with product and then disintegrates. Sebaceous glands are the classic example, releasing a lipid-rich sebum.
explanation.highYield: Holocrine = whole cell death; sebaceous gland.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Acne involves overactive sebaceous glands with holocrine secretion.

questions.question: Apocrine secretion involves:

options.explanation: Apocrine glands (e.g., mammary, some sweat glands) release product by shedding portions of the apical cytoplasm.

explanation.overview: In apocrine secretion, the apical portion of the cell containing the secretory product is pinched off and released. This occurs in mammary lipid secretion and in some sweat glands (axillary, perianal).
explanation.highYield: Apocrine = apical cytoplasm pinches off; mammary (lipid) and axillary sweat.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Apocrine glands are the source of malodor in axillae.

questions.question: Which epithelial type is found in the proximal convoluted tubule of the kidney?

options.explanation: Proximal tubule cells are simple cuboidal with prominent microvilli (brush border) for reabsorption.

explanation.overview: The proximal convoluted tubule is lined by simple cuboidal epithelium with an extensive brush border of microvilli, maximizing reabsorption of glucose, amino acids, ions, and water.
explanation.highYield: Proximal tubule = simple cuboidal + brush border; major reabsorption site.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Acute tubular necrosis often affects proximal tubule cells, leading to sloughing and blockage.

questions.question: The epithelium of the vagina is:

options.explanation: The vagina is lined by non‑keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which provides protection and undergoes hormonal changes.

explanation.overview: The vagina is lined by non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which is estrogen-responsive and accumulates glycogen, fostering Lactobacillus and an acidic pH.
explanation.highYield: Vagina = non-keratinized stratified squamous; glycogen-rich under estrogen.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Atrophic vaginitis results from thinning of this epithelium after menopause.

questions.question: What type of epithelium lines the trachea?

options.text: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar with goblet cells
options.explanation: The trachea is lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells, forming the mucociliary escalator.

explanation.overview: The tracheal epithelium is a classic pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium, with goblet cells, ciliated cells, basal cells, and brush cells. It traps particles in mucus and sweeps them upward.
explanation.highYield: Trachea = pseudostratified ciliated columnar + goblet cells; mucociliary clearance.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: In smokers, this epithelium often undergoes squamous metaplasia, impairing clearance.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of simple epithelia?

options.explanation: Simple epithelia consist of a single cell layer, ideal for absorption, filtration, and secretion.

options.text: Only found in ducts of glands

explanation.overview: Simple epithelium has one layer of cells resting on a basement membrane, serving absorption, secretion, filtration, and diffusion.
explanation.highYield: Simple epithelium = one cell layer; classification by shape.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Mesothelioma arises from simple squamous mesothelium.

questions.question: Stratified epithelia are primarily involved in:

options.explanation: The multiple layers of stratified epithelia provide protection against mechanical and chemical abrasion.

explanation.overview: Stratified epithelia have multiple layers, with the deepest layer constantly proliferating and the superficial layers sloughing off, making them ideal for protection from abrasion.
explanation.highYield: Stratified = protection; classified by surface cell shape.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Pressure ulcers (bedsores) develop when stratified epithelium breaks down.

questions.question: The junctional complex at the apical end of epithelial cells includes:

options.explanation: Near the apical surface, epithelial cells have a junctional complex consisting of tight junctions, adherens junctions, and desmosomes.

explanation.overview: The apical junctional complex consists of the tight junction (zonula occludens), the adherens junction (zonula adherens), and the desmosome (macula adherens) in that order from apical to basal.
explanation.highYield: Junctional complex: tight junction → adherens junction → desmosome.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Disruption of junctional complexes by pathogens allows bacterial invasion.

questions.question: The glycocalyx on the apical surface of epithelial cells is composed of:

options.explanation: The glycocalyx is a carbohydrate-rich coating of membrane glycolipids and glycoproteins involved in cell recognition and protection.
Lipids are in the membrane, but glycocalyx is carbohydrate.

explanation.overview: The glycocalyx (cell coat) is a fuzzy layer on the apical surface, composed of the carbohydrate portions of membrane glycoproteins and glycolipids, involved in protection, adhesion, and recognition.
explanation.highYield: Glycocalyx = glycoproteins + glycolipids; cell coat.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Glycocalyx damage in the intestinal epithelium is implicated in inflammatory bowel disease.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of simple epithelium?

options.explanation: Pseudostratified is classified as simple (all cells touch basement membrane).
Stratified squamous is a stratified epithelium; the others are simple (pseudostratified is considered simple because all cells contact the basement membrane).

explanation.overview: Simple epithelia have one layer; stratified have multiple. Pseudostratified is a type of simple epithelium where all cells rest on the basement membrane.
explanation.highYield: Simple: squamous, cuboidal, columnar, pseudostratified. Stratified: squamous, cuboidal, columnar, transitional.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Classification of epithelium is important in histopathology.

questions.question: The epithelium lining the gallbladder is:

options.explanation: The gallbladder is lined by simple columnar epithelium specialized for water absorption and concentration of bile.

explanation.overview: Gallbladder mucosa has tall simple columnar cells with microvilli and abundant mitochondria, adapted to absorb water and concentrate bile. No goblet cells normally.
explanation.highYield: Gallbladder = simple columnar, no goblet cells; concentrates bile.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Cholecystitis can lead to metaplastic changes, including goblet cells.

questions.question: Which cell junction is connected to actin filaments?

options.explanation: Adherens junctions attach to the actin cytoskeleton and form a belt-like adhesion around the cell.
Tight junctions are linked to actin but are not primarily anchor junctions.

explanation.overview: Adherens junctions (zonula adherens) form a continuous adhesion belt around epithelial cells, linking to the actin cytoskeleton via cadherins and catenins.
explanation.highYield: Adherens junction = actin filaments + cadherins; apical belt.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Loss of E-cadherin in adherens junctions promotes tumor invasion.

questions.question: Keratin is a type of intermediate filament found in:

options.explanation: Keratin intermediate filaments are characteristic of epithelial cells, providing mechanical strength.
Blood cells mainly have vimentin or none.

explanation.overview: Keratin (cytokeratin) intermediate filaments are the hallmark of epithelial cells. Different keratin types are expressed in different epithelial subtypes, useful for tumor typing.
explanation.highYield: Keratin = epithelial intermediate filament; used as immunohistochemical marker.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Carcinomas are keratin-positive, distinguishing them from sarcomas (vimentin) and lymphomas.

questions.question: Which of the following is a unicellular exocrine gland?

options.explanation: Goblet cells are individual mucus-secreting cells found scattered in epithelial linings.

explanation.overview: Goblet cells are the only unicellular exocrine glands in the human body. They are modified columnar cells that secrete mucin into the lumen of the respiratory and GI tracts.
explanation.highYield: Only unicellular gland = goblet cell; mucus secretion.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Increased goblet cells (hyperplasia) in airways occurs in chronic bronchitis.

questions.question: The epithelium of the seminiferous tubules in the testis is:

options.explanation: Seminiferous tubules are lined by a complex germinal epithelium that is pseudostratified in appearance.

explanation.overview: The seminiferous epithelium is a specialized stratified epithelium (sometimes called germinal epithelium) with Sertoli cells and developing spermatogenic cells at various stages, giving a pseudostratified appearance.
explanation.highYield: Seminiferous tubules = complex germinal pseudostratified epithelium; Sertoli + spermatogenic cells.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Disruption of this epithelium leads to infertility (e.g., Sertoli-only syndrome).

questions.question: Which of the following epithelia is best described as 'stratified cuboidal'?

options.explanation: Sweat gland ducts are lined by stratified cuboidal epithelium, which is two layers of cuboidal cells.

explanation.overview: Stratified cuboidal epithelium consists of two or more layers of cuboidal cells. It is rare, found in ducts of sweat glands and large exocrine glands.
explanation.highYield: Stratified cuboidal = ducts of sweat glands; two layers.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Rarely, carcinomas can exhibit stratified cuboidal differentiation.

questions.question: The function of stereocilia (long microvilli) in the epididymis is:

options.explanation: Stereocilia in the epididymis are long microvilli that increase surface area for fluid absorption.
Epididymal epithelium secretes some substances, but stereocilia primarily increase absorption.

explanation.overview: Stereocilia are extremely long, non-motile microvilli found on the pseudostratified columnar epithelium of the epididymis and ductus deferens. They increase surface area for fluid absorption, concentrating sperm.
explanation.highYield: Stereocilia = long microvilli; epididymis; fluid absorption, NOT motility.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Dysfunction of the epididymal epithelium can impair sperm maturation.

questions.question: Which layer of the skin is composed of keratinized stratified squamous epithelium?

options.explanation: The epidermis is keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.
It's a membrane, not a layer.

explanation.overview: The epidermis is the outermost layer of skin, a keratinized stratified squamous epithelium composed mainly of keratinocytes. It continually renews from the basal layer.
explanation.highYield: Epidermis = keratinized stratified squamous epithelium.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Basal cell carcinoma arises from the basal layer of the epidermis.

questions.question: The epithelium lining the cornea is:

options.explanation: The anterior corneal epithelium is stratified squamous, non‑keratinized, providing a smooth refractive surface.

explanation.overview: The corneal epithelium is a non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium about 5-6 layers thick. It is transparent and serves as a barrier while providing a smooth optical surface.
explanation.highYield: Corneal epithelium = non-keratinized stratified squamous; transparent.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Corneal abrasions damage this epithelium; healing is rapid if the basement membrane is intact.

questions.question: What is the main function of the glycocalyx?

options.explanation: The glycocalyx is involved in cell‑cell recognition, adhesion, and protection.

explanation.overview: The glycocalyx is a carbohydrate-rich layer on the cell surface that mediates cell-cell recognition, adhesion, and provides a protective barrier. It also contains enzymes and contributes to immune evasion.
explanation.highYield: Glycocalyx = recognition, adhesion, protection; carbohydrate coat.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Pathogens (e.g., influenza virus) interact with the glycocalyx to attach to cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of exocrine glands?

options.text: They secrete products onto surfaces via ducts
options.explanation: Exocrine glands secrete their products through ducts onto epithelial surfaces.

options.text: They are derived from connective tissue

explanation.overview: Exocrine glands release their products (enzymes, mucus, sweat, etc.) through a duct system onto an epithelial surface. They are classified by duct structure and secretory unit shape.
explanation.highYield: Exocrine = ducts, onto surface; Endocrine = no ducts, into blood.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Obstruction of exocrine ducts (e.g., gallstones, kidney stones) causes gland dysfunction.

questions.question: A gland with a branched duct and flask‑like secretory units is called:

options.explanation: A compound acinar (alveolar) gland has a branched duct and multiple acini. Example: salivary glands.
Tubuloacinar has both tubules and acini.
Sweat glands are simple coiled tubular.

explanation.overview: Compound glands have branched ducts; acinar secretory units are flask-shaped. Salivary glands (parotid, submandibular) are compound acinar. Pancreas is compound tubuloacinar.
explanation.highYield: Compound acinar = branched duct + acini; e.g., salivary glands.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Salivary gland tumors often arise from the ductal or acinar cells.

questions.question: Myoepithelial cells are found in:

options.explanation: Partially correct, but also in salivary and lacrimal glands.
Myoepithelial cells surround secretory units of sweat, mammary, lacrimal, and salivary glands, and contract to expel secretions.
They are found in several glands.

explanation.overview: Myoepithelial cells are contractile cells of epithelial origin located between the basal lamina and secretory cells of acini and intercalated ducts in certain exocrine glands (salivary, sweat, mammary, lacrimal).
explanation.highYield: Myoepithelial cells = contractile, help expel secretion; salivary, sweat, mammary.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Myoepithelial cells are used to distinguish in situ from invasive carcinoma in breast pathology.

questions.question: Which type of epithelium is found in the renal collecting ducts?

options.explanation: Collecting ducts of the kidney are lined by simple cuboidal epithelium.

explanation.overview: The collecting ducts of the kidney are lined by simple cuboidal epithelium, which gradually becomes columnar as the ducts approach the renal papilla.
explanation.highYield: Collecting ducts = simple cuboidal to columnar; ADH-responsive.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Principal cells in collecting ducts are targets of ADH (vasopressin) and aldosterone.

questions.question: The function of cilia in the respiratory epithelium is to:

options.explanation: Cilia propel mucus (with trapped debris) toward the throat, where it is swallowed or expectorated.
Mucus is secreted by goblet cells.

explanation.overview: Respiratory motile cilia beat in coordinated waves, propelling a layer of mucus upward toward the pharynx, clearing inhaled particles and pathogens (mucociliary clearance).
explanation.highYield: Respiratory cilia = mucociliary escalator; clear particles.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Ciliary dysfunction (e.g., in smoking, CF, PCD) causes recurrent infections.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a modification of the apical surface?

options.explanation: Desmosomes are lateral junctions; the others are apical surface specializations.

explanation.overview: Apical surface specializations include microvilli, cilia, stereocilia, and the glycocalyx. Desmosomes are located on lateral surfaces, providing cell-cell adhesion.
explanation.highYield: Apical: microvilli, cilia, stereocilia, glycocalyx. Lateral: tight junctions, desmosomes, gap junctions.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Loss of apical microvilli in celiac disease is a histological hallmark.

questions.question: Simple columnar epithelium with goblet cells and microvilli is characteristic of:

options.explanation: Stomach has simple columnar but lacks prominent goblet cells and microvilli brush border.
The small intestine has simple columnar epithelium with goblet cells and a brush border (microvilli) for absorption.

explanation.overview: The small intestine's simple columnar epithelium consists of absorptive enterocytes with a striated border (microvilli) and scattered goblet cells. Villi and crypts are characteristic.
explanation.highYield: Small intestine = simple columnar + goblet cells + microvilli (striated border).
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Villous atrophy in celiac disease reduces absorptive surface.

questions.question: The epithelial lining of the ureter is:

options.explanation: The ureter, like the bladder, is lined by transitional epithelium (urothelium) that stretches.

explanation.overview: The entire urinary collecting system (renal calyces, pelvis, ureter, bladder, proximal urethra) is lined by transitional epithelium (urothelium).
explanation.highYield: Ureter = transitional epithelium; stretches.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Urothelial carcinoma can occur anywhere in the urinary tract.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the basement membrane?

options.text: It is secreted entirely by epithelial cells
options.explanation: The reticular lamina is from connective tissue.

options.text: It contains type IV collagen and laminin
options.explanation: The basement membrane consists of type IV collagen, laminin, entactin, and proteoglycans, providing support and filtration.

options.text: It is impermeable to all molecules
It is absent in blood vessels
It is a layer of connective tissue cells

explanation.overview: The basement membrane is a specialized ECM composed of type IV collagen, laminin, nidogen/entactin, and perlecan. It anchors epithelium and acts as a selective filter.
explanation.highYield: Basement membrane = type IV collagen + laminin; acellular.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Alport syndrome is due to a mutation in type IV collagen, causing kidney, ear, and eye defects.

questions.question: The brush border of proximal tubule cells is composed of:

options.explanation: Proximal tubule cells have numerous microvilli forming a brush border to increase reabsorptive surface area.

explanation.overview: The brush border of the proximal convoluted tubule is composed of densely packed microvilli, dramatically increasing the apical surface for reabsorption of filtrate components.
explanation.highYield: Proximal tubule brush border = microvilli; PAS-positive.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Fanconi syndrome results from dysfunction of proximal tubule transport, often with loss of brush border.

questions.question: Acinar cells of the pancreas are an example of:

options.explanation: Pancreatic acini are serous, secreting digestive enzymes in a watery fluid.
Mucous acini are pale, with flat nuclei.
Pancreas has both exocrine (acini) and endocrine (islets).

explanation.overview: Serous acini consist of pyramidal cells with basal basophilia (rough ER) and apical eosinophilic zymogen granules. They secrete a watery, enzyme-rich fluid. Pancreatic acini and parotid gland are serous.
explanation.highYield: Serous acini = dark-staining, basal RER, apical granules; pancreas, parotid.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Acute pancreatitis involves premature activation of zymogen granules.

questions.question: The epidermis of thick skin (e.g., palms) has an additional layer called:

options.explanation: Thick skin has a stratum lucidum, a clear layer between stratum granulosum and corneum, absent in thin skin.

explanation.overview: Thick skin (palms, soles) has all five epidermal layers: stratum basale, spinosum, granulosum, lucidum (translucent, eosinophilic), and corneum. Thin skin lacks a prominent stratum lucidum.
explanation.highYield: Stratum lucidum = thick skin only; palms and soles.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: The stratum lucidum is especially prominent in calluses.

questions.question: Which cell type is responsible for producing keratin in the epidermis?

options.explanation: Keratinocytes are the predominant cells of the epidermis, producing keratin.

explanation.overview: Keratinocytes make up about 95% of epidermal cells. They synthesize keratins, which form the intermediate filament cytoskeleton, and during terminal differentiation, they become corneocytes of the stratum corneum.
explanation.highYield: Keratinocyte = keratin production; main epidermal cell.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Psoriasis is characterized by rapid keratinocyte proliferation and abnormal differentiation.

questions.question: Melanocytes are derived from:

options.explanation: Melanocytes originate from neural crest cells and migrate to the epidermis.

explanation.overview: Melanocytes are derived from neural crest, migrating into the epidermis during embryonic development. They produce melanin and transfer it to keratinocytes.
explanation.highYield: Melanocyte = neural crest origin; melanin production; in stratum basale.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Malignant melanoma arises from melanocytes; it can metastasize widely.

questions.question: Langerhans cells are antigen‑presenting cells found in the:

options.explanation: Langerhans cells are dendritic cells located mainly in the stratum spinosum, involved in immune response.

explanation.overview: Langerhans cells are bone marrow-derived dendritic cells residing mainly in the stratum spinosum. They capture antigens and migrate to lymph nodes to present to T cells.
explanation.highYield: Langerhans cells = dendritic cells; stratum spinosum; antigen-presenting.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Langerhans cell histiocytosis is a clonal proliferation of these cells.

questions.question: Merkel cells are associated with:

options.explanation: Merkel cells are tactile epithelial cells associated with nerve endings for light touch sensation.

explanation.overview: Merkel cells are located in the stratum basale, especially in fingertips. They contain dense-core granules and synapse with afferent nerve endings, forming Merkel discs for fine touch sensation.
explanation.highYield: Merkel cell = tactile sensation; in stratum basale; neuroendocrine features.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Merkel cell carcinoma is a rare, aggressive skin cancer.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of epithelial membrane?

options.explanation: Basement membrane is an extracellular structure, not an epithelial membrane. Mucous, serous, and cutaneous membranes are epithelial membranes.

explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Arthritis involves inflammation of the synovial membrane.

questions.question: The serous membrane lining the pleural cavity is called:

options.explanation: Serous membranes are lined by mesothelium (simple squamous epithelium).
That's the sac around the heart.

explanation.overview: Serous membranes (pleura, pericardium, peritoneum) consist of a simple squamous epithelium called mesothelium, resting on a thin layer of connective tissue, and secrete a serous fluid for lubrication.
explanation.highYield: Serous membranes = mesothelium (simple squamous) + connective tissue.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Mesothelioma is a malignancy of mesothelial cells, often caused by asbestos.

questions.question: Simple columnar epithelium with microvilli and goblet cells is found in the:

options.explanation: Stomach lacks prominent goblet cells and microvilli brush border.
The colon has simple columnar epithelium with many goblet cells for mucus secretion, but fewer microvilli than small intestine.

explanation.overview: The colon has a simple columnar epithelium with numerous goblet cells and absorptive colonocytes with short microvilli. It lacks villi, having a flat surface with crypts.
explanation.highYield: Colon = simple columnar, many goblet cells, no villi; microvilli shorter.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Ulcerative colitis affects the colon epithelium, causing goblet cell depletion.

questions.question: The function of the stratum corneum is:

options.explanation: Cell division is in stratum basale.
Keratin is produced in lower layers.

options.text: Barrier against water loss and pathogens
options.explanation: The stratum corneum consists of dead, keratinized cells providing a waterproof protective barrier.
Melanin by melanocytes in basal layer.
Sensory is by Merkel cells and nerve endings.

explanation.overview: The stratum corneum is the outermost layer of the epidermis, composed of dead, anucleate corneocytes embedded in a lipid matrix, forming the principal barrier to water loss and pathogen entry.
explanation.highYield: Stratum corneum = dead, keratinized cells; barrier function.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Defective barrier in atopic dermatitis (eczema) leads to dry skin and infections.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of endocrine glands?

options.text: They secrete hormones into the bloodstream
options.explanation: Endocrine glands are ductless and secrete hormones directly into the bloodstream.

options.text: They are derived from connective tissue

explanation.overview: Endocrine glands are ductless organs that release hormones into the interstitial fluid, which enter the bloodstream and act on distant target cells.
explanation.highYield: Endocrine = ductless, into blood; Exocrine = ducts, onto surface.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Endocrine disorders result from over- or underproduction of hormones.

questions.question: The respiratory epithelium of the nasal cavity is:

options.text: Pseudostratified ciliated columnar with goblet cells
options.explanation: The nasal cavity (except olfactory region) is lined by respiratory epithelium, which warms, humidifies, and cleans inhaled air.

explanation.overview: The conducting portion of the respiratory system, from nasal cavity to bronchi, is lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells, adapted for conditioning air.
explanation.highYield: Nasal respiratory epithelium = pseudostratified ciliated columnar + goblet cells.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Allergic rhinitis causes increased goblet cell secretion and ciliary dysfunction.

questions.question: Which epithelium is specialized for mechanical protection and is found on the surface of the tongue?

options.explanation: The tongue is covered by stratified squamous epithelium, which can be keratinized (filiform papillae) or non-keratinized.

explanation.overview: The dorsal surface of the tongue is lined by stratified squamous epithelium, which is keratinized over filiform papillae and non-keratinized elsewhere, protecting against abrasive food.
explanation.highYield: Tongue = stratified squamous; keratinized on filiform papillae.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Leukoplakia (white patch) on the tongue may represent hyperkeratosis or dysplasia.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of intercellular junction?

options.explanation: Lysosome is an organelle, not a cell junction.

explanation.overview: Cell junctions include tight junctions, adherens junctions, desmosomes, gap junctions, and hemidesmosomes. Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles involved in intracellular digestion.
explanation.highYield: Not a junction: lysosome (organelle).
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Lysosomal storage disorders are due to deficiencies in lysosomal enzymes.

questions.question: The epithelium lining the endocervix is:

options.explanation: The endocervical canal is lined by simple columnar mucus-secreting epithelium.

explanation.overview: The endocervix is lined by simple columnar epithelium with mucous cells. The transformation zone is where it meets the stratified squamous epithelium of the ectocervix.
explanation.highYield: Endocervix = simple columnar mucus-secreting; ectocervix = stratified squamous.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Cervical cancer arises at the squamocolumnar junction (transformation zone).

questions.question: Which of the following epithelia is found in the alveoli of the lungs?

options.explanation: Alveoli are lined by type I pneumocytes (simple squamous) for gas exchange.
Type II pneumocytes are cuboidal but produce surfactant.

explanation.overview: The alveolar walls are lined predominantly by type I pneumocytes, which are extremely thin simple squamous epithelial cells covering ~95% of the surface, permitting rapid gas diffusion.
explanation.highYield: Alveoli = simple squamous (type I pneumocytes) for gas exchange.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Damage to type I cells in ARDS leads to impaired oxygenation.

questions.question: What type of epithelium lines the external auditory meatus?

options.explanation: The external auditory canal is lined by skin (keratinized stratified squamous epithelium).
Middle ear and Eustachian tube have pseudostratified.

explanation.overview: The external auditory meatus is continuous with the skin and lined by keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, containing hair follicles and ceruminous glands.
explanation.highYield: External ear canal = keratinized stratified squamous; skin.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Otitis externa (swimmer's ear) is an infection of the skin lining the ear canal.

questions.question: Metaplasia of the bronchial epithelium from pseudostratified columnar to stratified squamous is most commonly caused by:

options.explanation: Allergy causes goblet cell hyperplasia, not squamous metaplasia.
Chronic irritation, especially from cigarette smoke, induces a change from respiratory to a more protective stratified squamous epithelium.
Vitamin A deficiency causes squamous metaplasia in other sites (e.g., cornea), but smoking is the primary cause in bronchi.

explanation.overview: Squamous metaplasia is a reversible change where one adult epithelium is replaced by another. In the bronchi, chronic irritation (smoking) transforms pseudostratified columnar epithelium into stratified squamous, which is more resistant but loses ciliary function.
explanation.highYield: Squamous metaplasia in bronchi = smoking; loss of ciliary clearance.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Squamous metaplasia is a precursor to squamous dysplasia and carcinoma.

questions.question: The endothelial lining of capillaries is:

options.explanation: Capillaries have the thinnest endothelium, a single layer of squamous cells, to facilitate exchange.

explanation.overview: Capillaries are composed of a single layer of endothelial cells (simple squamous) and a basement membrane, minimizing the diffusion distance for gases and nutrients.
explanation.highYield: Capillary wall = endothelium (simple squamous) + basal lamina.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Capillary leak syndrome involves increased permeability of this endothelium.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a compound tubuloacinar gland?

options.explanation: Sweat gland is simple coiled tubular.
The exocrine pancreas is a compound tubuloacinar gland, with serous acini and centroacinar cells.

explanation.overview: The pancreas has both tubular and acinar elements (centroacinar cells lining the beginning of ducts within the acinus), making it compound tubuloacinar.
explanation.highYield: Pancreas = compound tubuloacinar; parotid = compound acinar.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma arises from the ductal component.

questions.question: The cells of the stratum granulosum contain granules of:

options.explanation: Keratin is accumulated but not as distinct granules; the granules are keratohyalin.
Stratum granulosum cells contain basophilic keratohyalin granules and lamellar bodies, important for barrier formation.
Melanin is produced by melanocytes and transferred.

explanation.overview: The stratum granulosum is a thin layer of flattened cells containing basophilic keratohyalin granules (profilaggrin) and lamellar bodies (lipid-containing) that contribute to the skin barrier.
explanation.highYield: Stratum granulosum = keratohyalin granules + lamellar bodies.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Ichthyosis vulgaris is associated with reduced keratohyalin granules (filaggrin mutations).

questions.question: The epithelial lining of the fallopian tube is:

options.text: Simple columnar with ciliated and secretory cells
options.explanation: The oviduct is lined by simple columnar epithelium with two main cell types: ciliated (movement) and secretory (nutrient fluid).

explanation.overview: The fallopian tube mucosa has simple columnar epithelium with ciliated cells (helping move the egg) and non-ciliated peg cells (secretory). Estrogen stimulates ciliation.
explanation.highYield: Oviduct = simple columnar, ciliated + secretory; estrogen-dependent.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Ectopic pregnancy most commonly occurs in the ampulla of the fallopian tube.

questions.question: Which type of epithelium lines the ducts of most exocrine glands?

options.explanation: Mainly in large ducts near opening.
Small intercalated ducts are simple cuboidal; larger ducts may be simple columnar or stratified cuboidal/columnar.

explanation.overview: Exocrine gland ducts are lined by epithelium that varies from simple cuboidal (intercalated ducts) to simple columnar or stratified cuboidal/columnar (intralobular and interlobular ducts).
explanation.highYield: Duct epithelia: cuboidal → columnar as duct size increases.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Sialolithiasis (salivary stones) often obstructs Wharton's duct, causing swelling.

questions.question: The lamina propria is the connective tissue layer directly beneath the epithelium in:

options.explanation: In mucous membranes, the lamina propria is the loose connective tissue layer supporting the epithelium.
Serous membranes have a thin connective tissue layer but not called lamina propria.

explanation.overview: The lamina propria is a loose connective tissue layer under the epithelium of mucous membranes, providing support and housing blood vessels, lymphatics, and immune cells.
explanation.highYield: Lamina propria = connective tissue of mucous membranes; part of mucosa.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Inflammatory cells infiltrate the lamina propria in many mucosal infections.

questions.question: The olfactory epithelium is a specialized type of:

options.explanation: The olfactory epithelium is a pseudostratified columnar epithelium containing olfactory receptor neurons, supporting cells, and basal cells.

explanation.overview: The olfactory epithelium in the superior nasal cavity is a pseudostratified columnar epithelium with olfactory receptor neurons, sustentacular (supporting) cells, and basal stem cells. It lacks goblet cells but has Bowman's glands.
explanation.highYield: Olfactory epithelium = pseudostratified columnar; no goblet cells; olfactory neurons.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Anosmia (loss of smell) can result from damage to this epithelium (e.g., COVID-19).

questions.question: Which of the following glands uses apocrine secretion?

options.explanation: The lipid portion of milk is released by apocrine secretion, pinching off apical cytoplasm.

explanation.overview: Mammary glands release milk fat droplets by apocrine secretion, where a portion of the apical cytoplasm containing the lipid droplet is pinched off. The protein component (casein) is secreted via merocrine exocytosis.
explanation.highYield: Apocrine secretion: mammary lipid droplets, axillary sweat glands.
explanation.clinicalCorrelation: Apocrine glands in the axillae are responsible for body odor when secretions are metabolized by bacteria.
